newsitem.title: TURKEY: Rebel Kurds kill three postmen in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Rebel Kurds kill three postmen in Turkey.

text.p: Rebel Kurds on Monday launched a rocket attack on a minibus carrying postal workers in southeastern Turkey, killing three, state-run Anatolian news agency said.
It said two postal workers and the bus driver died in the attack in Van province.
The attack brings to 65 the number of people killed in the latest clashes in Turkey's 13-year-old conflict with guerrillas of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
The emergency rule region governor's office said on Monday that Turkish security forces had killed 60 Kurdish rebels in fighting in the southeast.
A statement said 50 guerrillas, members of the outlawed PKK, were killed in operations in the far southeastern province of Hakkari, eight were killed in Siirt province and two in Diyarbakir.
Two members of the security forces were killed and three wounded in the operations which began on Sunday night, it said.
More than 26,000 people have been killed in 13 years of conflict between the armed forces and the PKK, fighting for self-rule in the mainly Kurdish southeast.
